objects.original: Eq. (15) sums actual degree-p tensor contractions with Xi_i,p at one level of Xi in the full Euclidean direct sum.
objects.reconstructed: The function sums over p using coordinate (i,p,c) of the full flat Gaussian. Coordinate c assigns a basis entry to each ordered slot (r,j,l).
objects.evidence: There are p choices of r and K^j choices of l for each j from 0 through h-i, giving p S_i ordered slots and n^(p S_i) coordinate assignments. The product of the u_(i+j) entries is precisely the coefficient of psi_i^tensor p; taking the i,p slice with WithLp.toLp 2 does not alter entries.

domains.original: At i from 0 through h, the argument is a tuple in (S^(n-1))^(h-i+1), with even degrees 4,6,...,P and real Gaussian tensor coordinates.
domains.reconstructed: Finite index types for levels, degrees and slots; an arbitrary tuple in finite real Euclidean space restricted by norm one at every trailing position.
domains.evidence: The finite degree carrier is a subtype of Fin(P+1), with evenness and lower bound 4, so includes P and exactly the allowed degrees. Since i≤h, the Lean natural subtraction implements ordinary h-i. The unit-norm predicate is exactly the real sphere condition.

quantifiers.original: The paper chooses sufficiently large n and h=floor((log n)^(1/3)/32), then an arbitrary level and fixed trailing directions.
quantifiers.reconstructed: Every positive n and natural h, every level in Fin(h+1), and each deterministic tuple with unit norms, before taking the law over Xi.
quantifiers.evidence: On the paper parameter locus Lean specializes to the same quantifiers. Its wider n,h range is an explicit isolated-law generalization: finite carriers, the exact block law, unit feature, and Gaussian addition do not use the asymptotic depth relation. It does not widen the hard-family admissibility claim.

assumptions.original: The fixed directions are unit and the coefficient draw is the unconditioned joint standard Gaussian with independent source-degree blocks.
assumptions.reconstructed: Unit norms are the only proof premise; the probability law is specified as stdGaussian on the full Euclidean coefficient carrier. No independence, integrability or measurability hypothesis is added.
assumptions.evidence: jointCoefficientBlocks_hasLaw is actually called on the exact flat array and supplies the block product law. Evaluation gives each standard marginal, and angularDegreeComponent_hasLaw is actually called on that block with the given unit norms. Independence and moment existence are derived inside the proof.

conclusion.original: The implicit finite-sum consequence of the actual sum and adjacent one-degree laws is the centered normal with variance n sum_p a_i,p^2.
conclusion.reconstructed: HasLaw identifies the pushforward as the centered real Gaussian with the same variance and includes a.e. measurability.
conclusion.evidence: The proof uses mutual independence for Gaussianity and pairwise independence with finite second moments for exact variance addition. The focused test independently recovers the real variance and zero mean from the law. The variance is nonnegative by n≥0 and the squared amplitudes, so toNNReal introduces no truncation on the claimed value.

scopes.original: The uncropped scalar angular law at fixed deterministic directions under mu_n; spatial cutoffs, conditioned coefficients, and adaptive queries are distinct paper objects.
scopes.reconstructed: A scalar law for one fixed level and tuple, not a simultaneous field bound, not independence of repeated evaluations, and not a law for data-dependent directions.
scopes.evidence: The map varies only the coefficient draw. No C_i, U_i, beta_i, gate, or posterior occurs in the formal statement. Eq. (51) instead involves the radial, zero-extended fields, weighted sum across levels, and Gaussian exponential moment. Applying Fact 10 to those actual fields additionally needs the radial/degenerate identification; this theorem does not prove it or the conditional level iteration.

constant_dependencies.original: K=2^(74(h+1)); P=2^(64(h+1)); S_i=sum_(j=0)^(h-i) K^j; a_i,p=[p^4 S_i^2 sqrt((h-i+1) log(2 P S_i))]^(-1); scalar prefactor sqrt(n).
constant_dependencies.reconstructed: The decoder calls the 64-exponent cutoff K and the 74-exponent repetition base M, and uses the same natural log, square root, powers, and dimension factor.
constant_dependencies.evidence: Decoder K is source P and decoder M is source K; their uses, not their names, determine the match. The finite subtype adapter preserves the natural degree; j.val provides exactly the relative tensor exponent, the bound permits 4 and P, and natural-to-real casts in the amplitude and variance preserve the displayed values.
